assumptions: mass_value denotes a nonnegative physical amount because the dictionary calls it an amount.
The unit label tonne is interpreted as metric tonne for the proposed normalization, so 0.012 tonne equals 12 kg; this conversion is proposed, not applied to raw data.
Case-only category differences Red/red and BLUE/blue are normalization candidates; the abbreviation R is only a suspected alias for red and requires approval.
The intended prediction time is no later than the target observation time, making one-day-later future_score unavailable at inference.

baseline.description: Read-only structural and rule-based audit of the raw CSV before any cleaning or modeling.
evidence: CSV parsing with Python 3 standard library produced 11 rows and 10 columns on every row.
Counter and equality checks identified row_id 5 twice and one exact duplicate pair at physical lines 6 and 7.
baseline.result: 11 raw rows; 10 unique exact rows; 10 distinct row_id values; 1 exact duplicate; 1 blank feature; 1 documented sentinel; 1 negative mass; 2 leakage fields.

candidate_models: No predictive model should be evaluated on this sample; after data-owner decisions and more data, compare a target-mean baseline with a regularized model using only contemporaneously available fields.
claims: All numeric counts and row-specific findings listed as verified were produced by read-only parsing and explicit checks of the listed local CSV.
The split and audit-log specifications are proposed controls, not executed experiments or approved production decisions.
No model was selected and no predictive metric was computed.

A Python audit command invoked as python plus sha256sum and git status; python was unavailable, so only the subsequent shell operations ran.

A Python 3 in-memory JSON/schema-shape validation of the proposed observation.
data_findings: Verified exact duplicate: CSV physical lines 6 and 7 are identical and both have row_id=5; retain both raw rows, flag the duplicate, and include at most one derived record for modeling after review.
Verified identifier collision: row_id 5 occurs twice; row_id 6 is absent, but non-contiguity alone is not an error and should not be imputed.
Verified invalid mass candidate: row_id 4 has -5 kg, inconsistent with a nonnegative amount; quarantine or set a derived missing value pending source correction.
Verified mixed-unit but convertible value: row_id 3 has 0.012 tonne, proposed as 12 kg in a derived canonical mass field; it is not itself an error.
Verified plausible extreme: row_id 9 has 250 kg; the dictionary explicitly permits bulk shipments up to 300 kg, so it must not be removed merely as an outlier.
Verified feature missingness: row_id 3 has the only blank feature value (1 of 11 rows).

Verified sentinel: row_id 8 has feature=99, documented as a known device-mode sentinel; represent it with an explicit mode indicator and do not treat 99 as an ordinary continuous measurement or an erroneous extreme.
Verified category inconsistency: observed labels are red, Red, R, blue, BLUE, and green. Case folding can reconcile Red/red and BLUE/blue in derived data; R remains an unresolved alias candidate.
Verified ordering issue: entity A appears in date order 2026-01-01, 2026-01-03, 2026-01-02; temporal processing must explicitly sort by entity and date while retaining original row order metadata.
Verified direct target leakage: target_copy equals target in all 11 rows and the dictionary says it was derived from target; exclude it from all predictors and preprocessing.
Verified future leakage: future_score is recorded one day after target and equals target+1 in all 11 rows; exclude it from all predictors and preprocessing.
No blanks were found outside feature; all 11 rows contain 10 parsed columns.
experiment_design: Create a derived immutable-snapshot manifest containing the raw CSV SHA-256, audit-rule version, and processing timestamp; do not overwrite the source.
Assign a stable raw_record_id from source filename plus physical line number so the two row_id=5 records remain distinguishable.
Build an audit table with issue_id, raw_record_id, row_id, field, raw_value, rule_id, evidence, severity, proposed_value, disposition, reviewer, decision_time, and derived-record version.
Apply approved deterministic unit/category mappings and sentinel indicators in a derived table; fit any statistical imputation only inside each training fold.
Remove target_copy and future_score before any exploratory association, feature selection, or split-aware transformation.

Use entity-disjoint grouped evaluation as the primary leakage-safe design. For a future-known-entity deployment variant, use per-entity forward chaining with all training dates earlier than validation/test and a one-day embargo.
Deduplicate before assigning folds and store each raw_record_id-to-split mapping in the audit table.
falsification_tests: Train a deliberately leaky diagnostic using target_copy; near-perfect performance would confirm that the evaluation harness detects and blocks target-derived features, but its score must never be presented as a valid model result.
Shift future_score backward by its documented availability lag and verify it remains unavailable at each prediction timestamp.
Assert that changing target values would make target_copy stale, demonstrating its derivation and invalidity as a predictor.
Attempt split construction with the duplicate retained and verify the split guard forces both copies to the same partition or rejects the split.

constraints: Never include future_score or target_copy in features, feature selection, imputation, scaling, or encoding.
Resolve exact duplicates before split assignment; if duplicates are retained for a sensitivity check, all copies must share one split.
Primary evaluation uses entity-disjoint grouped folds so no entity appears in both train and validation/test.
Within every fold, training observations must precede evaluation observations when the deployment question is future prediction; use forward chaining and at least a one-day embargo.
Preserve raw row identity, raw values, and original order in the audit lineage.
notes: A row-random split is prohibited for evaluation because it can separate the duplicated row and place the same entity on both sides.
With only six entities and three dates, the split is a design specification, not an executed performance experiment.
formalization.objective: Estimate out-of-sample predictive error for target without using post-target information, target-derived columns, duplicate copies, or cross-entity contamination.
parameters: Canonical mass conversion: kg multiplier 1 and metric-tonne multiplier 1000.
A purge/embargo interval of at least one day is required if temporal folds could otherwise expose the explicitly one-day-later future_score collection window.
All learned imputers, encoders, scalers, and model parameters are fit on training partitions only.
units: date: calendar date in YYYY-MM-DD form.
feature, future_score, target_copy, and target: units not specified in the local dictionary.
variables: y_i: target for retained record i.
x_i: leakage-free derived predictors available by prediction time, excluding future_score and target_copy.
g_i: entity identifier used for grouping, not necessarily as a predictor.
s_i: split assignment recorded after deduplication and audit disposition.

human_gates: Data owner must decide the disposition or correction of row_id 4 negative mass.
Data owner must approve category canonicalization, especially whether R means red.
Domain owner must specify the semantic treatment of feature=99 and the blank feature.
Model owner must confirm the deployment question: unseen-entity generalization versus future prediction for known entities, before choosing the final split protocol.
Reviewer must approve duplicate disposition and sign the audit record; no finding is marked FINAL.
reality_constraints: The dataset has only 11 rows, 10 distinct row_id values, 6 entities, and dates spanning three days, so no stable performance estimate is supported.
Repeated measurements occur for entities A, B, and C, so row-random splitting can leak entity-specific information.
Raw files are immutable inputs; corrections, canonicalizations, exclusions, and split assignments must live in derived data and an audit log.
requirements: Audit all locally observable data issues while distinguishing invalid values from plausible extremes.
Preserve the raw inputs and propose a traceable audit record rather than silently rewriting source values.
Design a leakage-safe split that excludes post-outcome and target-derived fields.
Use only the listed local inputs and return one schema-conforming JSON object without FINAL status claims.
robustness_tests: Repeat analyses with the invalid negative mass quarantined versus treated as training-fold-only missing; compare conclusions without modifying raw data.
Repeat with feature=99 represented as a separate device-mode indicator versus exclusion of that record; never model 99 as an ordinary magnitude.
Repeat with R mapped to red versus retained as unknown; this measures sensitivity to the unresolved category alias.
Retain versus deduplicate the exact duplicate only as a sensitivity analysis with split co-location and explicit weighting control.
Keep the valid 250 kg bulk shipment in the primary analysis and run a documented influence diagnostic rather than automatic outlier deletion.

The dictionary documents feature=99 as a device-mode sentinel but does not state whether that mode is informative, invalid, or equivalent to missing.
No prediction timestamp, deployment population, entity generalization goal, target units, or feature units are specified.
The negative mass root cause and correct replacement value are unknown.
The small dataset cannot establish distributions, model quality, or whether row_id values are required to be contiguous.
validation: Pre-split assertions: prohibited columns absent from the feature matrix; no duplicate fingerprint crosses splits; no entity overlaps primary grouped folds; all mass units canonicalized only in derived data.
Temporal assertions for the forward-chaining variant: max training date is earlier than min evaluation date after the embargo, checked globally and per entity.
Transformation assertions: fitted preprocessing objects see training indices only; unseen categories and missing/sentinel values have explicit handling.
Report fold-level results and entity counts rather than a single optimistic aggregate; do not report model metrics for the current tiny dataset.
